rules.statement: When a regex validates or extracts a number that is passed on to another system (an API path, a CLI argument, an identifier), match digits with `[0-9]` rather than `\d`, because .NET `\d` also matches non-ASCII Unicode digits.
rules.why: With `\d`, malformed input such as Arabic-Indic digits passes validation, then fails later in the host call and produces misleading state.
rules.check: Look for `\d` in .NET or PowerShell regexes that parse numbers, IDs or counts for later use. Report it unless the pattern uses RegexOptions.ECMAScript or the input is meant to accept Unicode digits.

rules.statement: Don't ask a test to drop or shorten exact-phrase checks on instruction or documentation text as brittle when the suite checks those texts by phrase presence throughout and other tests cover the behavior: changing only those checks would make them the one exception to the suite's convention.
rules.why: The pinned phrases guard the wording each copy of the text must carry, and that wording is what its readers (agents) act on. Behavior is tested separately.
rules.check: Before reporting a wording-pinned assertion, look at how the sibling checks in the same test file verify text (for example, a shared phrase-presence helper), and check whether another test or fixture already covers the behavior.
